Dinto Under Fire for Continuing to Use Kim Soo Hyun’s Image in Japan Despite Contract Termination

By Hyun Eunsoo
hyun@frame-less.co.kr
Published: June 17, 2025 | Updated: June 19, 2025

Kim Soo Hyun Fronted Dinto’s Global Push — Especially in Japan

In August 2024, Dinto named actor Kim Soo Hyun as its official model in a bold move to expand its presence in both domestic and global beauty markets.

The brand launched aggressive campaigns in Japan — including photocard giveaways and pictorial-driven marketing — through LOFT stores, Qoo10 Japan, and various offline events, earning widespread attention.

March 2025: Contract Terminated — But His Image Still Circulates

On March 15, 2025, following controversy surrounding Kim Soo Hyun’s private life, Dinto officially announced the termination of his endorsement contract, stating it could no longer uphold the brand’s values and consumer trust.

Yet, even months later, Kim’s images remained visible across Dinto’s Japanese retail outlets and online platforms — still being used as of June 2025.

Photo: Local Japanese store (June 15, 2025)
Dinto Japan Homepage (June 15, 2025) – via X @nuyoos216

"Removed in Korea, Still Active in Japan" — Accusations of Double Standards

While Dinto swiftly removed Kim Soo Hyun’s images from its Korean website and social media after the contract termination, Japanese marketing materials were left unchanged. This prolonged exposure has sparked suspicion that it may not be a mere oversight, but rather a deliberate decision.

Some fans speculate that Dinto is continuing to benefit from Kim’s strong popularity in Japan, accusing the brand of adopting a "wait-and-see" strategy. Critics argue this undermines the meaning of the contract termination and may be viewed as misleading to consumers.

Dinto’s Silence Raises Ethical Questions

Dinto has yet to issue any official statement regarding the continued use of Kim Soo Hyun’s image in Japan. If this is not just a delayed update, the situation raises broader concerns about ethical brand management and inconsistent practices across markets. Restoring consumer trust may prove to be a growing challenge.

Whatever sympathy might have remained due to her passing has now completely evaporated. The truth is out, and it’s more devastating than expected: Kim Sae-ron repaid kindness with betrayal. She was never a victim—she was manipulative, self-centered, and ruthless, just like the family enabling her even in death.

Her text to Kim Soo-hyun begging for time and promising repayment, only to turn around and post a dating photo to manipulate public opinion, is proof of her two-faced behavior. That photo—posted amid financial turmoil and lawsuits—wasn't an accident. She later admitted her motive: “I wanted revenge. I wanted to die together.” She knowingly triggered dating rumors and dragged Kim Soo-hyun into her scandal, risking his career and mental health.

She pretended to be grateful. She promised to recover and work harder. But her actions exposed her intent—she was desperate to shift blame and hurt others when she couldn’t get her way.

At the time she sent those emotional texts, she wasn’t even dating Kim Soo-hyun anymore—she had already moved on to a drama PD 16 years her senior. Yet she resurfaced a past photo with Kim to stir trouble. The worst part? Her side then falsely accused Kim Soo-hyun of harassing her and leaking contacts—claims now proven false. The leaked text was not from him.

This wasn’t a mistake. This was calculated emotional sabotage.

Now, her family and Ga Se-yeon face legal action. Kim Soo-hyun’s side has filed defamation and false accusation lawsuits, and rightfully so.

The narrative has changed. Kim Sae-ron wasn’t a victim—she weaponized sympathy.
We stand with Kim Soo-hyun. 🖤
